full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the defendant-petitioner Md. Hasan Bali, Chairman, Saidkati Union Parishad, PS Banaripara, Dist. Barisal was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 30-1-97 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 101 of 1991 affirming those dated 23-3-91 passed by the Assistant Judge, Banaripara in Title Suit No. 69 of 1987 should not be set aside. 

 4. The Assistant Judge, Banaripara by judgment and order dated 23-3-91 decreed the suit. The defendant-petitioner preferred Title Appeal No. 101 of 1991 and by order dated 30-1-93 the Subordinate Judge affirmed the judgment and order passed by the Assistant Judge, Banaripara holding that the proceeding was not started as per Rules and the plaintiff was not served with the second show cause notice and as against that the defendant-petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 "that a suit for declaration that the order of dismissal from service was illegal and not binding without asking for any consequential relief for enforcing the declaratory decree was not maintainable and the omission to pray for any consequential relief for the purpose of enforcing the declaratory decree would be hit by the proviso to section 42, Specific Relief Act." 

 9. Mr. Syed Ziaul Karim, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party, submits that in the matter of suspension and ultimate dismissal of the plaintiff from service the chairman of the union parishad did not comply with the mandatory provision laid down in rule 10 of the Union Council (Village Police Force) Rule, 1968 because though rule 10(b) provides that when proceeding has been initiated by the chairman, enquiry into charges against the delinquent shall be held on receipt of the explanation from the delinquent. In the instant case admittedly the enquiry was held and conducted prior to the submission of the reply to the show cause notice by the delinquent dafadar. In the instant case the dafader was suspended on 15-8-87 and was asked to show cause within 7 days. The dafader replied to the show cause notice on 22-8-87 but inquiry was held on 10-6-87, 28-6-87 and 30-6-87 in contravention of rule 10. Mr. Ziaul Karim further submits that the order of dismissal was not preceded by any second show cause notice as required under rule 10(4). It is true that the enquiry into the charge against the delinquent dafader was held prior to the submission of his reply to the show cause notice and that no second show cause notice was served upon the dafader before he was dismissed from service but facts remain that to maintain a suit against Union Parishad a notice under section 78 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 which is a prerequisite was not served. The said notice is not a mere formality, it is a prerequisite for filing a suit against the Union Parishad as has been decided in the case reported in 1989 BLD 59. The learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of his second contention has referred to a decision reported in 47 DLR 173 in the case of Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation vs. Abdul Halim Chowdhury, wherein it was held that plaintiff''s prayer for declaration that he is still in service was not followed by any consequential relief and, as such, the court committed no illegality in holding that the omission to pray for such a relief for the purpose of enforcing the declaratory decree was hit by section 42 of the Act. But Mr Syed Ziaul Karim argued that the case reported in 47 DLR 173 is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case inasmuch as the requirement for consequential relief is applicable only in a case where the relationship between the parties is one of master and servant. But we are unable to accept his contention because the case reported in 1988 BCR page 44 was not a case between master and servant and that there it was held that omission to pay for consequential relief for enforcing declaratory decree would be hit by the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and that decision was upheld by the Appellate Division as has been referred to in 47 DLR 173. 

 10. In view of the facts, circumstances and the materials on record, I hold that the courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision in decreeing the suit in the face of the fact that the plaintiff did not serve any prior notice upon the union parishad as contemplated under section 78 of the Local Government (Union Parishads) Ordinance, 1983 and for omission to pray for consequential relief for enforcing declaratory decree the judgment and order passed by the Assistant Judge, Banaripara in Title Suit No. 69 of 1987 affirmed by the Subordinate Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No.101 of 1991 call for interference by this court. 

 11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without however any order as to costs. The Judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 101 of 1991 affirming those dated 23-3-91 passed by the trial Court are set aside.
